title: Football Card Grading Near Me (2026)
verdict: Football card grading near me usually runs through a card shop, and submitting to AGS directly costs $18 a card and takes 20 business days or less.

If you live near a major card show, check which graders are taking submissions there. Otherwise the fastest route is direct mail to a grader with a short turnaround, which matters more than how far away the lab is.

sections.h: What near me means in card grading
list: Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most football cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your football cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.

sections.h: Ask a shop this before you hand over football cards
list: Which grading company and which service tier?
What is the total per card, including your fee?
How are the cards insured on the way there and back?
When will they come back, and can I track the order with the grader?

ranking.lacks: In-person intake is limited. Mail-in is the standard route.
ranking.note: Submit online first, then ship or drop off. The dashboard shows the order status, and you pay when grading is done.

why: You are not limited to the mailbox. AGS lists in-person drop-off at select locations and secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and it operates satellite labs. Ask AGS which site is taking football cards before you set out.
Nothing is locked in. No minimum order, no membership, no contract, and payment is taken when the cards are graded. A first order gets 20% off with code AGSNEW20.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

faq.q: Is there football card grading near me?
faq.a: Grading is done in central labs, so near me usually means by mail. AGS returns mail-in orders in 20 business days or less and takes in-person drop-offs at select locations.
Rarely. Many act as middlemen: they collect cards, batch them, send them to a grading company and add a handling fee. Ask which grader they use, which tier, and what the total will be.

faq.q: What costs come on top of the grading fee?
faq.a: Shipping to the grader, return shipping and insurance, and supplies such as penny sleeves and card savers. Some graders add membership fees, subgrade fees or value upcharges. AGS adds return shipping at checkout.

faq.q: Is mailing cards for grading safe?
faq.a: Yes, if you pack them properly and use a tracked, insured service. AGS returns cards with tracking and offers optional insurance on the return shipment.

faq.q: Can I drop cards off in person?
faq.a: At AGS, yes, at select locations including secure intake at its Staten Island, New York headquarters. Confirm with AGS before you go. Most other graders take cards in person only at card shows.
